messages:
Marta Ruiz: Quick brainstorm: instead of inline text or a top toast, what if we surface compact error chips (small pill with ! icon) inline to avoid vertical shift and show an accordion-level summary banner? Need keyboard and SR friendliness.
Asha Verma: Ooh I like the chips idea for density. They don't add height if we position them absolutely to the input row. Popover on focus/hover for full message.
Noah Rivera: chips sound sleek but two concerns: 1) absolute positioning can overlap on very narrow windows, 2) SRs might not discover popovers.
Ellie Wong: accessibility notes: chips must still be in the tab order (button) and popover content should be reachable via aria-controls/aria-expanded. Also provide aria-live region for the accordion banner so SRs get a summary when panels open.
Marta Ruiz: agree. Implementation plan: error chip = <button aria-describedby="err-123-summary" data-error-chip> with visible icon and sr-only full text; popover shows extended message. For collapsed accordion we show a subtle red banner at the top of that accordion listing counts ("2 errors") with anchor links to chips.
Asha Verma: nice. That lets users scan which sections have issues. For keyboard-only users: Tab to banner, press Enter to focus first error chip inside. Could also have a "jump to next error" keyboard shortcut.
Noah Rivera: Shortcut is powerful but more of a power-user feature. If we add it, make it discoverable in the keyboard help menu. Also ensure we don't conflict with browser shortcuts.
Ellie Wong: SR flow: when user submits and there are errors in a collapsed accordion, open the accordion, move focus to the banner, announce "2 errors in this section" via role=alert, then user can Tab into chips. That avoids race conditions.
Marta Ruiz: copy for chips should be terse: "Required" or "Invalid email". Popover contains full helper + link to docs if needed. For required-field markers: should we still surface a small legend or inline postfix?
Asha Verma: since chips indicate errors, required-state should be separate. Propose a tiny persistent postfix "Required" for the first field in a group only, but only for groups where many fields are mandatory. Otherwise use a compact label like (req).
Noah Rivera: prefer a machine-readable attribute too: data-required=true so tests can validate. Also provide :focus-visible styles for chips and inputs that meet contrast.
Ellie Wong: destructive actions: we discussed typed-confirm vs undo before. Variant idea: for destructive in-scope items (non-customer-data) use an "are you sure" modal with a checkbox "I understand" + undo toast. For irreversible operations keep typed-confirm but reduce friction by pre-filling the token in a small copy area so the user still types it.
Marta Ruiz: pre-fill token? that lowers safety. Maybe show token but require typing it manually. Pre-filling in hidden field is dangerous. Keep manual typing. Keep copy concise: "Type delete-pool to permanently remove pool 'X' (id: 42)".
Asha Verma: UX nit: make the typed token monospace and include a small copy button to copy token for assistive tech users who can't type easily, but only enable copy after the user confirms they understand risk (tiny progressive disclosure).
Noah Rivera: that seems complex and could be abused. I'd rather have an optional accessibility flow: if user triggers an "accessible mode" we provide alternatives (confirm with voice or admin override). For now keep typed-confirm + accessible support doc.
Ellie Wong: Accessibility checklist for this pattern: 1) chips must be keyboard focusable; 2) popover content reachable and has role=document; 3) accordions open programmatically and set focus to banner with role=alert; 4) aria-invalid on fields; 5) data-required attributes for automation.
Marta Ruiz: toast collisions: chips/popovers reduce need for global toasts, but we still have undo toasts. Keep single-toast visible rule: undo has mid priority, errors are shown inline via chips so not queued.
Asha Verma: dev note: chips should avoid layout shifts by using CSS transform translate instead of changing flow. Test on very small widths and with long labels.
Noah Rivera: once mocks are up could we run a quick keyboard-only usability with 3 users? I can coordinate.
Ellie Wong: +1. I'll draft SR test steps covering: submit with collapsed panels, focus landing on banner, tab into chips, popover readout, and typed-confirm flow.
design-bot: Filed: https://go.redwood/design/issues/CI-901 "Compact error chips + accordion banners + a11y test plan". Assigned to @Marta and @Asha.
Marta Ruiz: solid. I'll mock 2 flows: (A) error chips + accordion banners + popovers, (B) inline tiny markers + top-level summary banner with anchor links. Will include keyboard shortcut opt-in as separate proposal. Mock links by EOD next Wed.
Asha Verma: thanks all, will help with copy and micro-interaction notes.
Noah Rivera: will schedule quick usability.
Ellie Wong: drafting test steps now.
Marta Ruiz: closing the thread, will post Figma once ready. :thumbsup:
